First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we need to find the hyperbolic identities that correspond to the following trigonometric identities: 

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{csch}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x},\,\,\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Then, we use the above identities to express the integral as

$$
{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{csch}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\  & =-\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)+\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =-\frac{2}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}}+\frac{2}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{4-{4}^{-1}}+\frac{2}{2-{2}^{-1}} \\  & =-\frac{8}{15}+\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
